units.source_text: 天氣寒冷，揹著揹包的肩膀也痠痛了很久，之後我在小提琴聲的吸引下，推開一家咖啡館的店門。

en.t: It was cold, and my shoulders had been aching for some time from carrying my backpack; later, drawn by the sound of a violin, I pushed open the door of a cafe.

units.source_text: 店裡的老闆娘總覺得有點面熟，詢問之後才知道，原來她就是十年前京橋那位小酒館的老闆娘。

en.t: The woman who ran the place looked somehow familiar, and when I asked, I learned that she was the proprietress of that little bar in Kyobashi from ten years earlier.

units.source_text: 她似乎也馬上想起了我，我們彼此都頗為吃驚，然後相視而笑。

en.t: She seemed to remember me at once too, and we were both rather startled, then looked at each other and laughed.

units.source_text: 我們沒有按當時的寒暄習慣，詢問彼此遭遇空襲燒燬的經歷，而是相互誇耀般地說道：「你是真的一點沒變啊。」

en.t: Instead of following the customary greetings of the time and asking each other about being burned out in the air raids, we spoke as if boasting to one another: "You really have not changed at all."

units.source_text: 「沒有啦，老了，都變成老太太了。

en.t: "No, not at all. I have aged; I have turned into an old woman.

units.source_text: 一身老骨頭都快要散架了呢。

en.t: These old bones of mine feel as if they are about to fall apart.
You are the one who looks truly young."

units.source_text: 「哪裡哪裡，我都有三個小孩了。

en.t: "Not at all, not at all. I already have three children.
